title: Two Fates: Scalding Water or Two Gardens

paragraphs.text: The refrain continues: "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" On the Day when the sky is split open, no man or jinni will need to be questioned about his sins, because everything will already be clear. The criminals will be recognized by the marks on them, and they will be grabbed by their forelocks and their feet. It will be said that this is the Hell which the criminals used to deny. They will move back and forth between the Fire and scalding water that has been heated to the greatest degree. After each of these frightening scenes, the same question is asked again, so that the listener keeps thinking about his Lord's favors.

In contrast, for anyone who feared standing before his Lord, there will be two gardens. Such a person was aware, during his life, that one day he would stand before Allah, and this awareness guided his actions. His two gardens have wide, spreading branches. In each of them, two springs flow freely, and in each there are two kinds of every fruit. The people there will recline on beds lined with thick silk brocade, while the fruit of the two gardens hangs low, close enough to pick easily. Between each of these descriptions, the refrain comes back again and again: which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? The rhythm of the passage is very powerful. A short description is given, then the question is repeated, then another description follows. This pattern makes the reader stop after every single blessing and think about it, instead of rushing past it. In this way, the passage calls the reader to gratitude for every favor of his Lord, the Most Merciful.

hardWords.m: hair on the front of the head
thick cloth with raised designs, often of silk
